enrolledNamespaces.description:
EnrolledNamespaces are the namespaces Themis acts on; alerts about others
are rejected.

bearerTokenFile.description: BearerTokenFile holds the token Alertmanager must send as a bearer token.

url.description:
URL is where Alertmanager reaches the intake, for the setup steps
Themis shows. The chart sets it to the core's Service.

tokenSecret.description:
TokenSecret names the Secret, in Themis's namespace, whose intake key
holds the token, for the setup steps Themis shows. The chart sets it.

intake.description: Intake configures how alerts reach Themis.

bearerTokenFile.description: BearerTokenFile holds the token investigators must send as a bearer token.

disabled.description:
Disabled means no investigator is installed: Themis collects evidence
and runs its checks, then each incident waits for a fix suggested by a
person or a tool outside Themis.

investigators.description: Investigators configures access to the gRPC API.

bearerTokenFile.description:
BearerTokenFile holds the admin token. It stays usable when people sign
in through OIDC, as a way in if the identity provider is down.

passwordFile.description:
PasswordFile holds the password. It is read at each try, and never
stored.

secret.description:
Secret names the Secret, in Themis's namespace, whose password key
holds it, for the command the sign-in page shows. The chart sets it.

initialAdmin.description:
InitialAdmin lets the first admin sign in with a generated password, to
make the first admin account. Set it or AdminAccount, not both.

passwordHashFile.description:
PasswordHashFile holds the password's hash: argon2id in the PHC string
format, or bcrypt.

passwordFile.description:
PasswordFile holds the password itself, for secrets tools that can't
hash it. Themis hashes it, and uses it only when the hash file doesn't
exist.

adminAccount.description:
AdminAccount is an admin account Themis makes at startup when no admin
account exists. Set it or InitialAdmin, not both.

redirectURL.description: RedirectURL is Themis's /auth/callback as the browser reaches it.

usernameClaim.description: UsernameClaim names the ID token claim used as the username (email).

groupsClaim.description: GroupsClaim names the ID token claim listing the person's groups (groups).

scopes.description:
Scopes are asked of the provider; openid is always added. Some
providers need groups to send groups, and some refuse it (openid, email,
profile).

sessionTTL.description: SessionTTL is how long a sign-in lasts (8h).

oidc.description: OIDC lets people sign in to the UI through an identity provider.

items.description: AccessBinding gives a role to people by username and by group.

access.description:
Access gives people roles, by username or group. Someone signed in who
matches no binding can't see anything.

api.description: API configures access to the HTTP API and the UI.

bearerTokenFile.description: BearerTokenFile holds the token the executor requires.

executor.description: Executor is where approved actions run; without it Themis never writes.

bearerTokenFile.description:
BearerTokenFile holds a token sent as a bearer token, if the receiver
needs one.

webhook.description: Webhook receives a JSON POST for every escalation.

externalURL.description: ExternalURL is where people reach the UI, for links in notices.

keyFile.description:
KeyFile holds the secret that encrypts secret settings, such as the
model's key. Losing it loses them; changing it makes them unreadable.

settings.description: Settings are those made in Themis's setup, kept in its database.

apiKey.description: APIKey says the install gives the investigator a key.

model.description:
Model is what the install itself set for the investigator's model, so
setup leaves those alone. The chart sets it.

serviceAccount.description: ServiceAccount is its identity, as namespace/name.

namespaces.description: Namespaces are those whose incidents it may read and suggest fixes for.

capabilities.description: Capabilities are the fixes it may suggest.

perMinute.description: PerMinute bounds its requests to suggest a fix. Defaults to 6.

ceiling.description:
Ceiling is the most sensitive evidence it may read: internal, or
sensitive to include container logs. Defaults to internal.

items.description: ProposalSource is one agent, known by its Kubernetes ServiceAccount.

sources.description: Sources are the agents allowed to suggest fixes.

window.description:
Window is how long an incident Themis couldn't decide stays open for a
suggestion. Defaults to 15m with sources, and to none without.

externalProposals.description: ExternalProposals lets callers outside Themis suggest fixes.

namespace.description:
Namespace is Themis's own. An IncidentProfile here applies to every
enrolled namespace; one elsewhere applies only to its own namespace.

resources.description:
Resources reads profiles and global settings from custom resources,
instead of the profiles below.

disabled.description:
Disabled names the packs to turn off: their profiles and checks are
left out.

scenarios.description:
Scenarios are the scenario packs Themis ships, each with its own
profile.

kubernetes.description:
Kubernetes is the Kubernetes metrics API (metrics.k8s.io), which
metrics-server serves: what containers use now, with no history. On
unless disabled; where the cluster doesn't serve it, the status page
says so.

address.description:
Address is the server's base URL, under which /api/v1/query is
served, for example http://prometheus-operated.monitoring:9090.

bearerTokenFile.description:
BearerTokenFile holds a token sent as a bearer token, if the server
needs one. Read on every query, so rotation needs no restart.

caFile.description:
CAFile holds the certificates that sign the server's, when the system's
don't.

certFile.description:
CertFile and KeyFile are a client certificate, for a server that asks
for one. Set both or neither.

insecureSkipVerify.description: InsecureSkipVerify accepts any certificate. Only for trying Themis.

prometheus.description:
Prometheus is a server answering Prometheus queries: Prometheus,
Thanos, Mimir, VictoriaMetrics or Grafana Cloud. It has history, so
it also answers peak memory and CPU throttling.

metrics.description:
Metrics says where Themis reads how much memory and CPU containers
use.

name.description: Name is a DNS label, for example rollout-regression.

priority.description:
Priority orders the profiles matching the same alert, highest first:
the first is the incident's primary profile. Every one that matches
applies. Unique, from 1.

alertNames.description: AlertNames lists the alertname values that match.

labels.description: Labels must all be present on the alert with these values.

targetKinds.description: TargetKinds lists the resolved target kinds that match, as Kind.group.

match.description: Match decides which alerts belong to this profile.

initial.description: Initial templates are collected before the investigation starts.

allowed.description: Allowed templates may be requested during the investigation.

evidence.description: Evidence lists the templates investigations of this profile may use.

checks.description:
Checks are the checks this profile runs, by name; none means every
check Themis has.

capabilities.description:
Capabilities are the remediations proposals may name; none means
diagnosis only.

justifiedBy.description:
JustifiedBy names, for each fix in Capabilities, the checks that
justify it: Themis refuses the fix unless one of them is true for the
incident, whoever suggests it. Each must be a check the profile runs.

guidance.description:
Guidance tells the investigator, in plain words, when this profile's
fixes are right and when they are wrong. It guides; checks and policy
decide.

investigation.description: Investigation bounds each investigation; zero fields take defaults.

items.description: PolicyRule decides when its CEL expression holds.

policy.description: Policy decides whether proposed actions run, wait for approval, or not.

window.description: Window is how long to watch the target after an action.

stability.description: Stability is how long the target must stay healthy within the window.

verification.description: Verification measures an action's outcome; zero fields take defaults.

items.description: Profile is one incident class and the alerts that belong to it.

profiles.description:
Profiles classify alerts into incident classes; an incident gets every
profile its alert matches, highest priority first. One named like a
scenario pack's profile replaces it.

title: Themis configuration
description: Config is the root of the configuration file.
